query_original: What is DRS and how does it work?
query_reformulada: What are the operational parameters of the Drag Reduction System (DRS) feature in accordance with Article 27.2 of the FIA Formula One Technical Regulations, and what specific aerodynamic benefits does its activation provide to a competing vehicle?
resposta:
The Drag Reduction System (DRS) was a feature that allowed drivers to reduce drag on their car's rear wing by opening a flap, increasing straight-line speed and providing an overtaking advantage. However, it has been removed from Formula 1 for the 2026 season and replaced with an "active aerodynamics" system.

According to Article C3 of the 2026 FIA Formula One Technical Regulations, the primary objectives of the regulations are to promote close racing by minimizing the aerodynamic performance loss when one car follows another, and to ensure aerodynamic performance remains compatible with the required operation performance of the Power Unit (PU).

The new active aero system will involve movable front and rear wings, designed to increase cornering speeds with the standard 'Z-Mode'. However, the operational parameters of this system are not specified in the provided context.

It is worth noting that the original DRS system allowed for a speed increase of 10-12 km/h (6.2-7.5 mph) by the end of the activation zone, but its exact aerodynamic benefits and operational parameters are uncertain without further information from the FIA regulations or technical documentation.
